open: Humid air, river light, wooden colonial facades, palms and a crowd already gathering around four World Tour tables near the Waterkant.
Wildcard steps out with the group. He is looking around more cautiously than usual.
A LOCAL ORGANIZER approaches and greets them in Dutch.
I hate flying. I also hate arriving somewhere and not knowing whether anyone understands me.
We have been travelling for a while.
But this? This feels... weirdly like home.

1: I can order food. I can ask directions. I can complain properly.
You complain fluently in every language.
This is different. They understand the details.
2: You have talked to six people already.
3: A SURINAMESE CONTENDER finishes another table nearby and exchanges easy jokes in Dutch with the crowd.
4: And I have not panicked once.
About cards or the flight home?
The route shifts toward Central Market. Food stalls, languages and smells collide. Wildcard is instantly distracted.
5: You said this would feel foreign.
6: You are rooting for the opposition now?
7: How many people have you met?
Enough that somebody just invited us to dinner.
8: Phones rise around Player. The Great Eight are recognized more quickly than they expected for the first South American stop.
The route speculation started before we landed.
The internet remains our greatest enemy.
9: The Surinamese contender closes the public tournament and is surrounded by friends and family.
Closer hands over the Keeper's Table card.
Night on the river. A private courtyard is lit warmly against old brick and dark water. The Surinamese Champion is already seated.
10: I thought home advantage might help.
You won Suriname. This table changes nothing about that.
Closer slides the World Championship invitation across.
Then I will see you again.
Later, Wildcard looks back at the riverfront.

open: Heat, horns, conversation, movement. Fans, tournament staff and street traffic all hit at once. A schedule board changes while Player is being stopped for photos.
A staff member rushes up: the entrance route has changed. Another points to a crowd blocking the planned path. A bag has gone to the wrong vehicle.

Before Player finishes: Closer redirects staff. Charmer speaks to the crowd. Scholar checks the new route. Sharp retrieves the bag. Optimist keeps the waiting players engaged. Wildcard finds the correct entrance. Jester distracts a livestreamer who is blocking the stairs.
We are getting worryingly good at this.

11: You do not talk much before you move.
12: A sudden crowd forms around Player after the match.
13: You have said that in every city.
That is because cities keep being good.
14: The Venezuelan contender wins a parallel match and watches how smoothly the Great Eight move through the crowd.
The second tournament block moves into a busier pedestrian district. Music, food, fans and street performers compete for attention.
15: A vendor recognizes Charmer from a clip online and starts talking as if they already know each other.
16: A minor power interruption briefly kills the tournament lights. Phones immediately become flashlights; Scholar and staff reset the table order.
17: I keep waiting for one of you to get in the other seven's way.
18: The contender changes tempo aggressively, trying to unsettle the surrounding tables.
19: The Venezuelan contender closes the tournament in front of a loud crowd.
Closer gives the Keeper's Table card.
Night above Caracas. The city glows below a private mountaintop salon. The Venezuelan Champion sits facing the Great Eight.
I watched all day. You cover for each other before the mistake happens.
20: I thought chaos would separate you.
Now we know where everyone lands.
Then I will learn the machine before Worlds.
Please stop calling us that. Scholar will build a dashboard.

open: Color, brick streets, mountain air and a growing crowd. Music spills from a nearby doorway.
We have been here eleven minutes.
Optimist notices a group dancing nearby.

21: Optimist asks a local woman if she wants to dance after the match.
22: A COLOMBIAN CONTENDER finishes another match nearby.
23: And I have met nine interesting people.
24: The Colombian contender wins again. Their friends pull Optimist into a conversation about the tournament.
Evening. Restaurants, music and groups gathering outside. The second set of tournament tables sits in a brighter nightlife atmosphere.
For every woman within fifty meters.
25: Optimist asks another woman to dance.
That was a no with scheduling.
26: The Colombian contender invites Optimist to sit with their card-playing friends between rounds.
27: You came here looking for romance and found a card club.
That is still a very good evening.
28: The contender wins again. The local group now cheers for both the contender and Player.
I have friends on both sides now.
That is not how competition works.
29: The Colombian contender wins the public tournament.
Across an ocean and nothing changes.
Bogota glows below. The Colombian Champion sits at a private terrace table above the city.
Good. You will need that at this table.
30: Okay. That one hurts more than the dance.
And that is why you get this.
The World Championship invitation is handed over.
Then next time, no dancing. Just cards.
The local card group calls Optimist over for one last photo.
Rejected three times. Leaves with twelve new friends.

open: Thin mountain air. Steep streets. The historic center rises and falls in every direction. Sharp walks quickly for half a block, then quietly takes a deeper breath.
At this altitude, more of it.

31: Sharp takes the stairs beside the tournament platform instead of the short lift.
He is altitude training between hands now.
32: Closer checks a running route on his phone.
A few kilometers. You can come.
33: Morning run. Closer keeps a measured pace. Sharp tries to push faster, then deliberately falls back beside him.
You can slow down without losing.
34: Back at the tournament, Sharp does push-ups during the break.
The second location sits higher with a wide view across Quito. Sharp stares at the stairs leading up.
35: A local contender notices Sharp stretching beside the table.
You train during a card tournament?
38: Sharp finishes another set of push-ups while the Ecuadorian contender wins nearby.
You know the cards do not care how many push-ups you can do.
39: The Ecuadorian contender wins the public tournament.
You look more tired than I do.
LEVEL 40 - KEEPER'S TABLE - HIGH ABOVE QUITO
The final table sits high above the city, lights spread beneath the Andes. Sharp is visibly tired, but focused.
No workout until after the match.
He said fine. Altitude changes people.
40: I found more to work on.
That is not always an invitation to double the workload.

open: The Great Eight arrive intending to scout tables. Within minutes, the first food recommendation derails the plan.
I heard there is a place around the corner -
We need a champion before dinner.
What if dinner finds the champion?

41: Immediately after the match, Charmer is handed a plate by a local vendor.
42: Scholar is explaining chifa history while eating.
43: A PERUVIAN CONTENDER quietly wins another table while the Great Eight debate their favorite dish so far.
44: Cut to the Great Eight eating again.
Ocean cliffs, Pacific air, paragliders and five more tournament tables along the Miraflores coast. The group arrives carrying food.
45: This might be the best food so far.
46: You are eating more than you are scouting.
48: A crowd asks Player for photos while Wildcard tries to protect a plate from being bumped.
Apparently mine are public property now.
49: The Peruvian contender wins the public tournament.
Night. Ancient adobe rises behind a private, warmly lit table. For once, nobody is holding food.

open: The Andes sit behind the city. Player barely gets through the hotel lobby before the first group asks for photos.
Your arrival was posted seventeen minutes ago.
We were still in the car seventeen minutes ago.

51: Player finishes the match and immediately gets surrounded for photos.
52: Player tries to buy coffee. Three people recognize them before the order is finished.
53: A CHILEAN CONTENDER wins nearby and watches Player navigate the crowd.
You play with more people watching than anyone here.
Then the cards should be the quiet part.
54: The second block is livelier. Street art, cafes and evening crowds. The fame problem is immediately worse.
They are waiting before we even put the tables down now.
55: A fan asks Player for a photo while another begins a livestream.
57: The Great Eight quietly form a buffer around Player without discussing it.
You do not have to do that.
58: Player finally gets a few quiet seconds and looks at the Andes instead of the phones around them.
59: The Keeper's Table card is handed over.
A private high-floor room. Andes silhouettes and city lights. No fans. No phones. Just the table.
Then enjoy it while you beat me.
60: I understand why they keep watching you.
The invitation is handed over. Player looks out at Santiago before the doors open and the noise returns.

open: Grand avenues, cafe culture, late-day warmth and music. Charmer looks comfortable before anyone says a word.

61: A local organizer greets Charmer warmly, then keeps talking long after the practical details are finished.
The city is flirting with him.
62: A BUENOS AIRES CONTENDER watches Charmer read the room before Player's match.
You watch people more than cards.
63: I think you have found your city.
64: Music drifts from a nearby tango demonstration. Charmer stops walking.
Cobblestones, antique stalls, cafe tables and tango dancers. Charmer is instantly pulled into a lesson.
Charmer takes the offered hand and learns a few steps surprisingly quickly.
This city really is flirting back.
65: The Argentine contender wins nearby, then joins the edge of the tango crowd without missing a beat.
66: You are enjoying the city too much.
We will see at the table.
67: Charmer gets pulled into another short dance between rounds.
69: The Argentine contender wins the public tournament.
I was hoping you would say that.
They are both flirting with the venue now.
A historic tango hall after hours. Red wood, mirrors, low lights. The dance floor has become a single card table.
70: You read it better than most.
Music starts again. Charmer looks toward the floor.
You do not have to tell me twice.

open: Old facades, cafes, bookshops and a slower waterfront rhythm. Scholar stops in front of a bookstore before the group reaches the first table.

71: Scholar finishes observing the match and immediately disappears into a nearby bookshop.
72: I will know after I read them.
73: A URUGUAYAN CONTENDER reads at a cafe table between rounds, mate beside the book.
74: Scholar finally speaks with the contender about the book instead of the match.
You came here for a tournament.
Late afternoon on the long waterfront. People sit with mate, talk, walk and watch the water. Five more tournament tables line a broad section of the promenade.
There is a literary cafe three blocks -
75: A local offers Scholar mate. He studies the ritual before accepting.
76: The Uruguayan contender wins again, then calmly returns to the same page of the same book.
78: Scholar buys a third book from a stall.
This is what happened to me with food in Lima.
79: The Uruguayan contender wins and closes the book.
Now we can talk about cards.
A private upper salon looks out across Montevideo. The Uruguayan Champion places a book beside the table before sitting.
80: You win. I still disagree with your book choice.
That is more offensive than the loss would have been.
The invitation is handed over. The Champion writes a book title on the back of a spare card and gives it to Scholar.

open: Warm evening, shaded plazas and groups sharing terere. Closer watches a circle pass the drink around while conversation slips between Spanish and Guarani.
You do not understand what they are saying.
But I think I know what they are talking about.
Closer answers a local organizer in Spanish. The organizer answers back naturally.
Here we go again. He learned another language.
I did not learn another language.
Italian helped. And we have been in South America for a while.
That is exactly how learning a language works.

81: Closer sits briefly with a local terere circle before the match.
82: A PARAGUAYAN CONTENDER notices Closer reading the group before anyone plays.
You watch the people before the cards.
84: The contender wins a parallel table, then joins the terere circle without making a show of it.
The second tournament block moves to the riverside. Sunset over the Paraguay River. The atmosphere is relaxed; the competition is not.
I will throw you in the river.
85: Closer orders in Spanish without noticing he did it.
You know you just did it again?
He does not even know anymore.
86: You listen more than you speak.
87: A quick exchange in Spanish passes between Closer and the contender.
I have facts. He has languages. It is uneven.
88: What do you like about it here?
89: The Paraguayan contender wins the public tournament.
LEVEL 90 - KEEPER'S TABLE - PARAGUAY RIVER TERRACE
Night on the river. Terere sits beside the table. The city glows behind the Paraguayan Champion.
90: Jester puts both hands over his face.
He is doing it on purpose now.
FINAL SOUTH AMERICAN STOP - RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL

open: Drums. Costumes. Music. Crowds. Rio is already in motion before the Great Eight reach the first tournament table.
This is my kind of place.
Do you remember the Cabin of Oddities?
I was living my best life in that room.
A Carnival group passes. Jester turns with them.

91: Jester returns wearing a feathered accessory he did not have five minutes ago.
92: Fun fact: capybaras are excellent swimmers.
That does not make every table a capybara seminar.
93: Player is recognized instantly and the crowd doubles.
94: Jester disappears into another Carnival group.
He knows where the next location is.
By evening, the World Tour tables are embedded in a sea of music and Carnival color. Jester returns in a full Carnival outfit.
We are not voting on the outfit.
95: A BRAZILIAN CONTENDER wins nearby and somehow stays completely focused despite the surrounding celebration.
Why would anyone do that right now?
96: Jester is pulled into a dance line and has to be physically redirected toward the tournament.
97: They can stay underwater for around five minutes.
You were going to say it anyway.
98: The Brazilian contender wins again. Jester celebrates with the local crowd as if he personally won.
You know I am playing against your group tomorrow?
99: The Brazilian contender wins the public tournament. Carnival erupts around the result.
So this is the last one in South America.
I want the full Great Eight.
Jester immediately gets pulled back toward the celebration.
LATER THAT NIGHT - INVITATION TO THE FINAL KEEPER'S TABLE
The Great Eight receive the time and private location. The Brazilian Champion will meet them later, away from the public tournament.
Everyone looks toward the Carnival crowd.
Do you want the honest answer?
A private salon overlooks the distant parade route. Drums can still be heard outside. Seven members of the Great Eight wait around the table. One chair is empty.
The BRAZILIAN CHAMPION enters, confident and relaxed.
I thought there were eight of you.
Closer looks at the empty chair.
100: RIO DE JANEIRO - 10 / 10 - SOUTH AMERICA CHAMPIONS 10 / 10
You won Brazil. This invitation was yours before you sat down here.
Closer slides over the World Championship invitation.
Then next time, bring all eight.

handoff: The seven begin gathering their things. The door suddenly opens. Jester walks in wearing the full Carnival outfit, feathers nearly scraping the frame.
Jester drops into the empty chair.
You were at Carnival this entire time?
I also learned that capybaras can stay underwater for around five minutes.
For the first time that night, all eight are together around the same table.
Let's head back and see where we stand.
Ten countries. Ten champions. We should look at the whole board again.
The mood shifts slightly. The World Championship field is growing, and the World Tour is moving toward its final shape.
But are we sure we have to leave tonight?
Sharp takes Jester by the shoulder and moves him toward the exit.
Rio at night. Carnival continues behind them as the Great Eight move toward the airport. Jester keeps looking back.
Later, the plane lifts away from the Brazilian coast.

Inside the cabin: Scholar reads. Sharp stretches in the aisle. Closer listens quietly. Optimist talks to someone across the aisle. Wildcard laughs. Charmer watches the lights disappear. Jester is still wearing part of the Carnival costume.
Player looks around at all seven of them, then out of the window.
South America is complete. Ten more champions have accepted the challenge. The Great Eight are heading back to the World Map to see what remains.
IF CONTINENTS REMAIN: SOUTH AMERICA COMPLETE - CHOOSE YOUR NEXT CONTINENT
IF FINAL CONTINENT: WORLD TOUR COMPLETE - 60 / 60 CHAMPIONS SELECTED

revisit.SOUTH AMERICA: The World Map fills the screen. Every completed continent remains lit.
SOUTH AMERICA - PREVIEWED - START SOUTH AMERICA / BACK
So we agree on the important part.
We are not routing a continent around rodents.
I still think it is a strong argument.
If we start South America, we finish South America.
commit.SOUTH AMERICA: SOUTH AMERICA SELECTED - ROUTE LOCKED UNTIL 100 / 100
The map zooms in. Ten stops illuminate.
PARAMARIBO - CARACAS - BOGOTA - QUITO - LIMA - SANTIAGO - BUENOS AIRES - MONTEVIDEO - ASUNCION - RIO DE JANEIRO
Wildcard looks at the route a little longer than the others.
That sounded like none of your business.

PLAYER.topic: PLAYER - SANTIAGO: THE CROWD NEVER STOPS
cues: Do you remember Santiago? You could not even sit down for ten minutes without a crowd finding you.

CLOSER.topic: CLOSER - ASUNCION: HE QUIETLY LEARNED SPANISH
cues: Do you remember Asuncion? You listened for a week and suddenly answered them in Spanish.
It was more than a week.
That is not helping your case.
This is exactly like Bogota. You got rejected and still came back with new friends.
That was a very good night.

CHARMER.topic: CHARMER - BUENOS AIRES: THE CITY FLIRTED BACK
cues: This feels like Buenos Aires again.
You said that last time too.

WILDCARD.topic: WILDCARD - SURINAME: FAR AWAY CAN STILL FEEL LIKE HOME
cues: Remember Suriname? You thought the other side of the world would feel completely foreign, then someone spoke Dutch.

JESTER.topic: JESTER - RIO: HE MISSED THE FINAL TABLE
cues: Do you remember Rio? We played an entire Keeper's Table without you because you were still at Carnival.

SCHOLAR.topic: SCHOLAR - MONTEVIDEO: BOOKS FIRST, TOURNAMENT SECOND
cues: This looks like Montevideo again. We came for cards and you are disappearing into a bookstore.

SHARP.topic: SHARP - QUITO: THERE IS ALWAYS MORE TO IMPROVE
cues: This feels like Quito again. You found one thing you could not dominate immediately and turned it into another workout.
That is exactly why I am reminding you.
